paragraphs: In [Chullin 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.43b.11), “Yonah, Zeira said: mevala’ta (מבלעתא).” Hyman reports that the Constantinople printing of the Rif has “R. Yonah אר״ז,” as cited in Dikdukei Soferim. He also reports that the halakhic authorities understood yonah as an actual dove rather than a sage’s name.[^2]

notes.text: The notice contrasts a personal name Yonah with yonah, “dove.” The consulted Chullin text and Rashi describe the swallowing passage; the Constantinople Rif reading remains Hyman’s report, not a new examination of that printing.

The linked Bavli places the words yonah and Zeira together in the discussion of the swallowing passage. [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Chullin.43b.11.5) explains mevala’ta as the site of swallowing. Hyman reports the Constantinople Rif reading and the interpretation of yonah as an actual dove.
